citation.title: AI Governance Engineering: The Thesis & Body of Knowledge

topics.name: Risk management
topics.summary: Identifying, analysing and treating AI risks across the lifecycle, and keeping the treatment current as the system and its context change.

topics.name: Governance and accountability
topics.summary: The policies, roles and accountability structures that put a named owner behind every AI decision and control.

topics.name: Impact assessment
topics.summary: Assessing an AI system's impact on fundamental rights, individuals and society before and during deployment.

topics.name: Data governance
topics.summary: Governing the data an AI system trains on and processes: lawful sourcing, quality, lineage and protection of personal and input data.

topics.name: Documentation and transparency
topics.summary: Technical documentation, disclosures and content labelling that make an AI system legible to regulators, deployers and users.

topics.name: Inventory and registration
topics.summary: Keeping an inventory of AI systems and agents and, where required, registering or filing them with the authorities.

topics.name: Logging and traceability
topics.summary: Automatic, tamper-evident logs and records that make an AI system's behaviour reconstructable after the fact.

topics.name: Human oversight
topics.summary: Human-in-the-loop checkpoints, approval gates and the ability to intervene in or stop an AI system.

topics.name: Runtime guardrails
topics.summary: Controls that constrain an AI system while it runs: input/output filtering, tool-invocation limits, isolation and memory management.

topics.name: Robustness, security and evaluations
topics.summary: Testing an AI system for accuracy, robustness, security and adversarial failure, including red-teaming and sandbox validation.

topics.name: Incident response and monitoring
topics.summary: Post-market monitoring, incident detection and reporting, and the complaint channels that surface real-world failures.

topics.name: Supply chain and third parties
topics.summary: Allocating responsibility along the AI value chain and managing risks from third-party models, data, tools and technical supporters.

topics.name: Prohibited practices
topics.summary: Uses of AI that a jurisdiction bans outright or a framework treats as unacceptable, and the intake controls that keep them out of the portfolio.

topics.name: Fairness and non-discrimination
topics.summary: Detecting and correcting bias in data, models and outcomes, and the lawful handling of the sensitive data that bias testing needs.

topics.name: Privacy and data protection
topics.summary: Lawful basis, minimisation, privacy by design and the privacy attacks specific to models, wherever an AI system touches personal data.

topics.name: Explainability and right to explanation
topics.summary: Explaining a model and an individual output to the people who use it or are affected by it, and the legal rights to an explanation and to contest.

topics.name: AI literacy and competence
topics.summary: Making sure the people who build, operate, oversee and use an AI system have the knowledge their role needs, with a record that shows it.

topics.name: Conformity assessment and certification
topics.summary: Demonstrating conformity before market entry, independent audit and certification, and the standards that carry a presumption of conformity.

topics.name: GPAI and foundation models
topics.summary: Duties that attach to general-purpose and foundation models themselves: documentation for downstream providers, evaluation, and systemic-risk management.

topics.name: IP and copyright
topics.summary: Lawful access to training content, honouring rights reservations, and keeping outputs from reproducing protected works.

topics.name: Agent identity and autonomy
topics.summary: Giving each agent its own identity and scoped permissions, bounding what it may do on its own, and keeping a human able to stop it.

topics.name: Content provenance and deepfakes
topics.summary: Marking synthetic content so it can be detected, labelling deepfakes for the people who see them, and verifying where content came from.

topics.name: Sandboxes and real-world testing
topics.summary: Supervised regulatory sandboxes and testing in real-world conditions, with the plans, consent records and reversal paths they require.

topics.name: Environmental impact
topics.summary: Measuring and reporting the energy and resource use of training and running AI systems, and weighing it in design decisions.

topics.name: Deployment, change and decommissioning
topics.summary: Putting a system into service, controlling changes that alter its risk, and withdrawing or retiring it safely when it no longer performs as intended.
